issues.legal_issue: An appeal does not lie from a merely procedural interlocutory order of the Rent Controller that does not affect a party’s rights or liabilities.
material_facts: A landlord sought eviction of a tenant on the ground of the landlord’s bona fide need for the premises.
The tenant alleged that the landlord had sufficient accommodation elsewhere and asked the Controller to appoint a commission to inspect that accommodation and prepare a plan.
The Controller refused to appoint the commission, noting that the landlord had been cross-examined about the accommodation and that a previous similar request had been refused.
The tenant appealed to the Rent Control Tribunal, which held that no appeal lay from the order; the High Court agreed.
issues.conclusion: The refusal to appoint a commission was a procedural interlocutory order that did not affect the tenant’s rights or liabilities, so no appeal lay to the Rent Control Tribunal under section 38(1). Any error in the order could be raised in an appeal from the final order in the eviction proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: Section 38(1) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, gives an appeal from an order of the Controller that affects a party’s right or liability, but its broad wording does not include interlocutory orders that merely regulate procedure and do not affect rights or liabilities. Sections 36 and 37(2) authorize procedural interlocutory orders; an interlocutory order under section 37(2) is appealable if it does affect a right or liability. Procedural errors may be raised in an appeal from the final order. The Court relied on Shankarlal Aggarwal v. Shankarlal Poddar, which construed similarly broad appeal language to exclude merely procedural orders that do not affect parties’ rights or liabilities.

rule.if: rent_control_proceeding and order_made_by_controller and order_is_interlocutory and order_only_assists_case_presentation and order_only_regulates_procedure and order_does_not_affect_rights_or_liabilities

predicates.rent_control_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the control of rent or eviction of a tenant.
predicates.order_made_by_controller: The Controller made the order during the proceeding.
predicates.order_is_interlocutory: The order was made before final adjudication of the proceeding.
predicates.order_only_assists_case_presentation: The order served only to assist a party in presenting the case in the pending proceeding.
predicates.order_only_regulates_procedure: The order regulated the procedure for conducting the proceeding and did not determine its substantive outcome.
predicates.order_does_not_affect_rights_or_liabilit: The order did not alter or determine any party’s rights or liabilities.

issues.definition: When a Controller makes an interlocutory order in a rent-control proceeding solely to assist presentation of the case and regulate procedure, without affecting any party’s rights or liabilities, an appeal from that order does not lie.
